title: William H. Crawford to James Monroe, Paris, 15 Aug 1813 (Despatch No. 3, item 1): a coded letter in the JQA code (catalogue 652)

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to France vol. 17, M34 roll 17 (naId 188672892), frames 0027R-0029R (catalogue 652)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the film. Monroe to Madison [ca. 1 Nov 1813] (PJM Pres. Ser. 7, Founders Madison/03-07-02-0011) says a coded letter "of the 4th of Sepr." (Despatch No. 4, frame 0031, which carries an interlinear decipherment) was to be deciphered; the PJM editors summarise the subjects of the coded letters of 15 Aug and 3 Sept (Madison/03-06-02-0671 n. 1) but print no deciphered text.

transcription.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (27 Oct 2026). About 150 groups (11%) re-read independently on fresh crops; one 0/8 slip corrected (29R01: 1383, not 1303). A review pass corrected one clear word (28R02: 'silly', not 'folly'). In this hand 8 is an o with a top tick. Measured with docs/_check_profile.py --measure --digits --drop-first (distinct counts mark variants such as 449o separately; 437 numbers).

system.summary: John Quincy Adams's numerical syllable-and-word code of 1811-1812 (the = 1385), about 1,600 numbers, rebuilt in ../jqa; used here unchanged.
system.sibling_key: the JQA code, ../jqa/code_table.tsv (rebuilt there from the State Department clerk's decodes and Ford's printed decipherments of JQA's 1811-1812 despatches), applied unchanged
system.notes: distinct_symbols = distinct groups in crawford1813_transcription.txt (python docs/_check_profile.py --measure --digits --drop-first; variants such as 449o counted separately; 437 numbers). unread_groups = distinct group numbers left in brackets in crawford1813_reading.md. Words in clear are written in among the groups.

prior_solution.where: A decipherment was made in 1813: Monroe to Madison [ca. 1 Nov 1813] (PJM Pres. Ser. 7, Founders Madison/03-07-02-0011) shows the letter was to be deciphered, and the PJM editors summarise the subjects of the coded letters of 15 Aug and 3 Sept (Madison/03-06-02-0671 n. 1); no deciphered text found, none on the film. ASP FR 3, the Crawford Papers and decoded copies elsewhere in RG 59 not checked (escalation print open). Correction 27 Oct 2026: the letter Monroe calls "of the 4th of Sepr. in cypher" is Despatch No. 4 of 3 Sept 1813 (frame 0031, deciphered between the lines), not this one; this letter is of 15 Aug 1813. A parallel independent reading by Brice Dudout was published the same day as this one (Europe chiffrée, 27 Oct 2026); neither used the other.

WAINUT contribution: first read with 1264 as 'and'; replaced by the full stop (30x, always at a clause end; 668 is 'and') after the Ellis 1839 alignment (../ellis1839). 713 = r gives Sir (27R02) and Mr. Warden (27R11), matching the PJM editors' mention of Warden. Context values 449 -nity (5x), 462 -tract (3x), 1106 will, 1323 been; about 40 context words marked [?].

WAINUT contribution: wrong-key controls (decode.py --controls): function-word rate 0.36 for the true table, 0.02-0.14 for shifts of 1-100, 0.03-0.05 for random table permutations; an independent bigram check gave 0.117 against 0.015-0.019 for shuffled group orders.

WAINUT contribution: Founders Madison/03-07-02-0011 and 03-06-02-0671 (PJM Pres. Ser. 7 and 6) say the letter came in cypher and summarise its subjects; no deciphered text printed; ASP FR 3 and the Crawford Papers not checked.
WAINUT contribution: read in part (crawford1813_reading.md, read_share 0.915).

WAINUT contribution: review pass: two passages (28R01-04, 29L08-29R01) decoded again with a separate script from origin/main ../jqa/code_table.tsv, same output; the clear word in 28R02 re-read on the full-resolution frame as 'silly', not 'folly' (no f descender), giving 'the silly pub[li]cations of our sapient Editors'; letters supplied in in[jur]ious and commu[nica]ted now marked.

Maintainer review: date checked on the frames. Legation register frame 0005 lists Despatch No. 3 (sent 19 Aug 1813) as "No 1 Letter from Minister to Secret.y of State Aug. 15th 1813 in cypher"; frame 0027 is headed "No (3)"; frame 0031 is Despatch No. 4, Paris 3 Sept 1813, with an interlinear decipherment. The letter is of 15 Aug 1813; the heading groups 932 939 932 954 read as the digits 1813 (Brice Dudout), not "force ow force 3rd". Group 9 (1303 here, 1503 Dudout) not settled at the size viewed.

Brice Dudout's parallel, independent reading published (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#crawford-1813): same table frozen; validated on No. 4's interlinear decipherment (194/226 and 224/246 values agree, shuffled-value controls at most 0.027/0.020); 1,330 of 1,371 groups read. Spot-checked against this reading: the same content (Dresden, the plan of indemnity, Barlow's capitalists, "sapient Editors"); not compared group by group.

texts.label: Crawford to Monroe, Paris, 15 Aug 1813 (Despatch No. 3) (catalogue 652), M34 roll 17 frames 0027R-0029R

reading_review.note: crawford1813_reading.md read in full as sentences 5 Nov 2026: coherent despatch prose throughout (why official talks with Bassano are deferred, a minister need not follow the court to Dresden, the plan of indemnities and the licences, the Adams cipher letter in the legation papers), with scattered holes marked [n] and [?word]; _check_reading scores it marginal (68 of 98 sentences clean, holes 0.102). Not checked against the images.

texts.summary: The new US minister in Paris explains why he has not opened official talks with Napoleon's foreign minister Bassano, who is with the Emperor at Dresden: Mr. Warden acts as the channel at Paris, a minister need not follow a court abroad, and Crawford has been painted as impetuous; the Russian mediation is unwelcome to Napoleon. He then judges Joel Barlow's secret plan to fund indemnities from trade licences useless, since licensed imports have glutted the American market.

texts.label: Crawford to Monroe, Paris, 15 August 1813: independent reading by Brice Dudout

reading_review.note: dudout/reading.md read as sentences 5 Nov 2026: coherent despatch prose throughout (Bassano's letter from Dresden, why official talks are deferred, the plan of indemnities, the licences, the Adams cipher letter among the legation papers); unread groups ‹n› and words restored from the sense [x] are scattered and none stops a sentence. Read in part under the strict 95% rule (87.9%).

texts.summary: In Paris since July 1813, the new United States minister waits for Napoleon, who stays at Dresden during the armistice. On Napoleon’s feast day he writes to the Secretary of State entirely in code: why he is not yet opening the negotiation, what he thinks of Bassano and of the Russian mediation, and above all the “plan of indemnities” he has just obtained privately from the foreign ministry — and the secret arrangement of his predecessor Joel Barlow with capitalists, which he decides to keep “entirely out of view”.
